messages.subject: code organization
parts:
quick question:

I want to do several plots with the same data and the same relatively
complicated set of transformations, scales, etc., but slightly
*different* y variables in each case.

For example, this might be the baseline plot:

g0 <- ggplot(beta_mix_tab,
aes(x=abund,y=value,colour=factor(st),
shape=factor(spcurve)))+
geom_point()+
geom_line(aes(group=interaction(spcurve,st)))+
scale_shape_discrete(name="rank-abund param")+
scale_x_log10(labels=trans_format('log10', math_format()))+
scale_colour_brewer(name="# sites",palette="Dark2")+
labs(x="local population size",y="beta (mean Jaccard dist)")
g0 + facet_grid(pmixcommon~pmixrare,label=label_both)

and in the next plot I would want to use y=value*st instead
of y=value.

I know how to use %+% to swap different sets of DATA into the same
plot, and to save the ggplot() components that add different scales,
faceting, etc. What I would like to do is something like:

GGSTUFF <- geom_point()+
geom_line(aes(group=interaction(spcurve,st)))+
scale_shape_discrete(name="rank-abund param")+
scale_x_log10(labels=trans_format('log10', math_format()))+
scale_colour_brewer(name="# sites",palette="Dark2")+
labs(x="local population size",y="beta (mean Jaccard dist)")

g0 <- ggplot(beta_mix_tab,
aes(x=abund,y=value,colour=factor(st),
shape=factor(spcurve)))+ GGSTUFF

but so far I don't have the right incantation for GGSTUFF (adding a
blank ggplot() at the beginning doesn't seem to work)

Any thoughts? If this isn't clear enough I can come up with a simpler
reproducible example but I thought it might be OK as is ...

Ben Bolker

messages.subject: Re: code organization
parts:
Would this do the trick?

GGSTUFF <- list(geom_point(),
geom_line(aes(group=interaction(spcurve,st))),
scale_shape_discrete(name="rank-abund param"),
scale_x_log10(labels=trans_format('log10', math_format())),
scale_colour_brewer(name="# sites",palette="Dark2"),
labs(x="local population size",y="beta (mean Jaccard dist)"))

b.
